newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soyoil hits new lows, soymeal also down.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soyoil hits new lows, soymeal also down.

text.p: Hot, rainy weather across much of the U.S. Midwest generated ideas about a bountiful new soybean crop and helped push all soyoil months to new contract lows Monday, traders said.
Soymeal futures were also lower at midsession.
U.S. forecasters indicated that the favorable soybean growing weather would extend through this week.
Supportive factors in Monday's trade included news that ADM was cutting back on its soybean crush operations.
CBOT floor traders also said that the soyoil market's lower prices would trigger export demand for U.S. product.
Some cash soymeal dealers noted a drop in demand from the livestock sector following the nation's summery temperatures. Animals typically eat less in hot weather, they noted.
In early trade, ABN Amro-Chicago Corp bought 200 lots December soymeal and Continental Grain bought 100 lots August, traders said.
In soyoil trade, ADM bought 100 lots July, Cargill sold 100 July and Term Commodities sold 100 August, traders said.

At 1140 CDT, July soyoil was down 0.11 cent a lb at 22.74 cents, and other months were 0.05 to 0.09 cent lower. July soymeal was $0.90 lower at $270.00 per ton. Other months were $0.50 to $1.60 lower.
